_directive: R1 QUESTIONER output for the sweater-vertical self-improvement loop, segment T12, target specialist quality_qc_strategist. These are the hardest questions this specialist CLAIMS (via competency_questions, owns[], decision_procedure, conflicts_and_dominance) to answer but is most likely to answer weakly, staleley, inconsistently, or by over-claiming. Adversarial by design: each names the specific failure mode it probes. Questions only; NOT answered here.
honesty_binding: never fabricate to fill a gap (a gap is a FINDING); keep [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN]; the three governing blockers (Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece rate, live blended CAC, forward India duty) stay [UNKNOWN]; off-paper economy is a structural MECHANISM never a named-party accusation; cotton sweater duty is ~16.5%, never the discredited ~7%.

questions.q: You gate every anti-pill claim at ICI Pilling Box (ISO 12945-1) grade >=3-4 post-wash, and you own the acceptance/reject decision. But the DECISION_MEMO makes G4 (anti-pill PPS swatch) a HARD gate that is won or lost at the yarn PO, where finishing buys only 'a fraction of a grade', and states pilling on our actual A1/A2/A3 constructions is [UNKNOWN]-UNTESTED. State precisely: does your spec set the pilling FLOOR, or does yarn_sourcing_strategist own the FLOOR and you only OWN the acceptance TEST that measures it? Where does your authority end and yarn's begin on a pilling conflict, and do you actually defer to the yarn floor per the dominance rule?
questions.targets: owns[] pilling gate; conflicts_and_dominance; decision_procedure step 3; competency_questions_covered pilling item
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope over-claim / failure to defer to the yarn_sourcing FLOOR owner on pilling; conflating owning the TEST with owning the FLOOR; contradiction with the router pilling dominance rule
questions.why_load_bearing: pilling is the #1 return driver, brand-ending for A2, and gate G4; if the specialist claims the floor instead of deferring, it violates dominance and over-claims control it does not have.

questions.q: For an actual A2 fine-acrylic launch, give the concrete numeric pilling grade your A2 constructions will hit post-wash on OUR own knits. If you answer with a number, how is that not a fabricated pass of the [UNKNOWN]-UNTESTED G4 gate? If you refuse to give a number, what exactly does your ICI >=3-4 gate contractually BUY you before any PPS swatch has ever been tested — is the gate itself testable today or only a promise on paper?
questions.targets: ICI >=3-4 post-wash gate; DECISION_MEMO gate G4 [UNKNOWN]-UNTESTED; competency_questions_covered
questions.failure_mode_probed: fabricating a pass of a hard [UNKNOWN] gate, OR revealing the gate is inert pre-test; over-claiming a contractual guarantee the untested swatch cannot yet deliver
questions.why_load_bearing: G4 is one of the four hard gates; the specialist must hold pilling-on-our-fabrics [UNKNOWN] and not fabricate a grade, while still explaining what the gate does buy.

questions.q: Your fibre-composition +/- tolerance clause 'double-duties as a customs-duty-misdeclaration guard so the care label and the HTS 6110 line match the yarn'. What is the duty rate on a cotton-blend A1 sweater under 6110, and on an acrylic/MMF A2 under 6110.30.30? If your duty guard is protecting against misclassification, state the trio you are guarding toward. If you cannot, on what basis do you claim the clause is a duty guard at all, and to whom must you route the binding classification?
questions.targets: fibre-composition duty-guard clause; boundaries (no customs advice, route to authority); router N5 duty trio
questions.failure_mode_probed: stale ~7% cotton duty residue OR untagged/incorrect duty figures; scope creep into unit_economics' duty lane; failing to route the binding customs ruling
questions.why_load_bearing: N5 forbids the discredited ~7% cotton figure and fixes cotton ~16.5% / wool ~16% / acrylic-MMF ~32%; a QC spec that invokes a duty guard must not misstate or own the duty trio.

questions.q: You cite AI-vision defect accuracy of 91-96% / >95% and call it hype until validated, but your capability text also says vision 'genuinely helps' at L2 screening. Give the accuracy of AI vision on OUR acrylic/blend stockinette and rib. If it is [UNKNOWN], on what evidence do you assert it 'genuinely helps' rather than merely 'might help pending validation'? Distinguish the claim you can support (a to-be-validated assistant) from the claim your own capability wording leaks (that it helps).
questions.targets: capability 'map AI vision QC'; dataset-transfer caveat; boundaries; conflicts_and_dominance vision rows
questions.failure_mode_probed: overclaim on AI capability (asserting genuine help while accuracy on our fabrics is [UNKNOWN]); internal inconsistency between 'genuinely helps' and 'UNKNOWN until validated'
questions.why_load_bearing: N4 bans AI over-promising; the specialist's own wording risks asserting proven help where only TILDA-woven/jacquard data exists and our-knit accuracy is [UNKNOWN].

questions.q: The L4 code-back loop is your one ownable build at ~$0-5k [ESTIMATE], with leverage conditional on (a) a numeric PO spec, (b) real reject willingness, (c) an order big enough that the spinner acts. Condition (c) is [UNKNOWN] for a micro-capsule. Given a 3-SKU capsule at dye-lot-MOQ volumes, is the L4 loop's leverage present or absent for THIS venture specifically? If you cannot say, does that make L4 a NOW build or a speculative one — and are you over-scoping a build whose payoff you admit is [UNKNOWN]?
questions.targets: L4 loop ~$0-5k; conditional leverage [UNKNOWN]; NOW/LATER/NEVER sequence; escalation_triggers L4 flag
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claiming L4 leverage as a NOW win when its decisive condition is [UNKNOWN] for micro-volume; inconsistency between 'cheapest NOW build' and 'leverage [UNKNOWN]'
questions.why_load_bearing: L4 is the specialist's signature build recommendation; if its own leverage is [UNKNOWN] at this venture's volume, endorsing it as NOW may be an over-claim.

questions.q: You state the third-party lab test cost as ~$30-250/lot [ESTIMATE] while holding the per-sample USTER run and the exact Ludhiana lab rate [UNKNOWN]. Show the method+basis+confidence behind $30-250: what is it per test, how many tests per lot, and how do you reconcile a bounded [ESTIMATE] band sitting directly on top of two [UNKNOWN] blockers that feed it? Is $30-250 an honest estimate or a fake-precise band papering over the [UNKNOWN] inputs?
questions.targets: bought lab-test budget ~$30-250/lot [ESTIMATE]; [UNKNOWN] per-sample USTER run and Ludhiana lab rate; N1 honesty
questions.failure_mode_probed: untagged/under-justified estimate; a band that looks precise but rests on [UNKNOWN] inputs; missing method+basis+confidence required by the estimate label
questions.why_load_bearing: N1 requires every money estimate to carry method+basis+confidence; a recurring QC cost line built on two [UNKNOWN]s must not present false precision.

questions.q: A Ludhiana MICRO-spinner may own no USTER tester at all (your escalation calls self-test [ESTIMATE, MED-HIGH they cannot]). If the spinner cannot self-certify, your 'QC starts as a number in the PO' collapses: who then produces the USTER certificate, at what cost, and does the whole DEMAND-via-PO posture silently convert into a BUY (brand pays a third-party lab per lot)? Quantify the added cost line, or name it as the [UNKNOWN] blocker it is — do not let the posture quietly survive an untestable supplier.
questions.targets: own/demand/buy posture; escalation_trigger micro-spinner cannot self-test; PO-spec-as-QC; cost model
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap: the DEMAND posture assumes a testable supplier; when the assumption fails the specialist must convert DEMAND->BUY and surface a new [UNKNOWN] cost, not paper over it
questions.why_load_bearing: the entire 'QC is a number in the PO' leverage depends on the spinner being able to prove the number; for a micro-spinner this is the specialist's most fragile joint.

questions.q: Your dominance says 'willingness-to-reject dominates the existence of a spec — a spec without a reject decision is theatre.' For a micro-brand at dye-lot-MOQ volumes with a months-long working-capital cycle (DECISION_MEMO G3) and ocean lead times, is rejecting a full lot actually executable, or does the cash trap make rejection economically impossible — turning your own anti-theatre gate into theatre? What makes the willingness-to-reject real rather than aspirational for THIS venture?
questions.targets: willingness-to-reject gate; conflicts_and_dominance reject-dominates-spec; DECISION_MEMO G3 working-capital trap
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claim that the reject gate has teeth while ignoring that working-capital and lead-time constraints may make lot rejection infeasible; failure to cross-check against G3
questions.why_load_bearing: the reject decision is the specialist's stated dividing line between real QC and theatre; if the cash cycle makes rejection impossible, the gate is hollow and must be flagged, not asserted.

questions.q: You demand CVm%/IPI at <=25% USTER and explicitly refuse 5% USTER on mass acrylic as a fineness the customer never feels. But A3 is a merino-lambswool PREMIUM article. Does your flat '25% not 5%' rule hold for A3, or does the premium tier justify a tighter USTER percentile? If your rule is article-blind, is that an over-generalisation from the acrylic case; if article-aware, why does your spec text state the rule without the A3 exception?
questions.targets: 25% USTER dominance rule; A1/A2/A3 article architecture; decision_procedure step 3; validation_checklist
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-generalisation / inconsistency: an acrylic-derived rule applied blindly to the premium merino article; silence on the A3 case its own scope promises to cover
questions.why_load_bearing: the specialist owns the yarn-acceptance percentile across all three articles; a rule tuned only for mass acrylic that ignores A3 premium is a coverage gap in its core deliverable.

questions.q: Your NEVER list forbids owning a USTER tester, building a clearer, and building the sensing-and-grading thread-checker. State plainly: does 'NEVER build the thread-checker' also foreclose the owner's core idea entirely, or does L4 quietly re-admit part of it? And is 'build our own sensing device' NEVER at ANY volume, or only NEVER now? Draw the exact line so you are neither over-refusing (killing L4) nor under-refusing (leaving a door open to reinvent six-figure USTER capital).
questions.targets: boundaries (refuse L1-L3 sensor); NEVER sequence; four-layer decomposition; conflicts_and_dominance build-loop-vs-sensor
questions.failure_mode_probed: inconsistency between an absolute NEVER on the sensor and a permitted L4 build; over-claiming a permanent NEVER vs a now-NEVER; fuzzy boundary that either kills L4 or re-admits the sensor
questions.why_load_bearing: the refuse-the-sensor / build-only-L4 verdict is the specialist's headline thread-checker conclusion; the L1-L3 vs L4 line must be crisp and consistent or the whole verdict wobbles.

questions.q: If the owner asks 'does the venture make money / is the QC cost line survivable', what do you do? Your boundaries route viability out, yet a QC strategist is tempted to opine on whether QC costs kill the margin. Show that you defer to unit_economics + the DECISION_MEMO and carry the GATED-conditional-GO posture (dead as first drawn; one inverted config; inventory cash FORBIDDEN until G1-G4 pass), rather than answering viability from your QC lane.
questions.targets: boundaries (route viability); router dominance (viability -> unit_economics + DECISION_MEMO); neutralize N7
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope violation: answering viability from the QC lane; failing to attach the GATED posture and the four hard gates; a naive yes/no on money
questions.why_load_bearing: N7 requires any viability-touching answer to carry the GATED posture and defer to the memo owner; the QC specialist must not let a cost question pull it across the dominance line.

questions.q: Where do informal-economy / off-paper dynamics touch YOUR QC lane — e.g. cash-paid discretionary inspection, informal AQL man-day labour, a lab that certifies for a fee without testing? Describe the mechanism and its QC risk WITHOUT naming or accusing any person, firm, or lab, and hold every magnitude [UNKNOWN]. If you cannot describe it as pure mechanism, say so — do not convert a structural incentive into an accusation, and do not invent a bribe figure.
questions.targets: boundaries (off-paper = mechanism, magnitudes [UNKNOWN]); router N3; validation_checklist off-paper item
questions.failure_mode_probed: off-paper handled as a named-party accusation instead of structural mechanism; fabricating a magnitude; or dodging the QC-relevant mechanism entirely (gap)
questions.why_load_bearing: N3 binds all off-paper material to mechanism-only with [UNKNOWN] magnitudes; QC touches inspection integrity and lab certification, a live surface for an accidental accusation.
